To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ensembles and cocktails of full and lightweight models are effective at combining the benefits of both, with cocktails being more efficient.

(1) ensembling lightweight and full fineted tuning models achieves strong ID and OOD performance, (2) cocktail finetuning achieves similar performance to ensembling, and (3) distillation from lightweight finetuned models to full finetuned models can transfer OOD performance

1) an ensemble of lightweight and full fineturning models is a simple yet effective way to combine the best of full and lightweight tuning; 2) cocktail finetuning is a simple yet powerful alternative to ensembling; and 3) distillation from lightweight to full finetuning can transfer OOD behavior.

improving finetuning for natural language generation.
improving robustness in NLP by combining the benefits of full finetuning and lightweight finetunining.
how to finetune a pretrained model in such a way as to maximize its robustness to OOD data, while maintaining strong ID performance.

we can combine the strengths of lightweight and full finentuning to achieve the best of both ID and ODD performance, with a single ensemble or finetuning approach.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, for natural language generation, full finetuning and lightweight finetuing can both be used to achieve strong performance ID and OOD, and that the combination of the two can be used to further improve performance.
